ai.overview: Michigan puts the Belt Holders lineal championship on the line for the first time in their current reign when they host Penn State on November 13, 2026. The Wolverines captured the belt in their most recent outing, a 5-4 road win at Ohio State, and now face a Nittany Lions squad struggling through a 2-5-1 season. With no committee involved, only the ice will decide who carries the belt forward.
key_matchups: Michigan's 8-1 record and four wins in their last five games against Penn State's 2-5-1 mark and recent 3-4 loss at Minnesota
The Wolverines' recent scoring form, putting up 5, 3, and 4 goals in three of their last five, versus Penn State's defensive struggles allowing 4 and 5 goals in recent losses
Michigan's 34-21-2 all-time edge in the series, including three wins in their last five head-to-head meetings
ai.betting_angles: Michigan enters as a clear Elo favorite with an 8-1 record and momentum from winning four of their last five games, while Penn State sits at 2-5-1 with just one win in their last five. The head-to-head history strongly favors the Wolverines at 34-21-2 all-time, and they've taken three of the last five meetings including a 5-2 win in their most recent matchup this past March. Penn State's road struggles and Michigan's home ice advantage further tilt the numbers toward the belt holder.
ai.prediction_writeup: Michigan's 8-1 record and strong recent form make them the clear choice to defend the belt in their first attempt. The Wolverines have shown they can win tight games, taking three of their last five by one goal including the 5-4 thriller that earned them the belt at Ohio State. Penn State arrives at 2-5-1 and coming off a 3-4 loss at Minnesota, continuing a season where they've struggled to find consistency. The all-time series edge of 34-21-2 and Michigan's home ice should be enough for the Wolverines to keep the belt and begin building a reign.
